stem: Two Massachusetts pharmacists reach opposite conclusions on the same drug utilization review question. One relies on a current peer-reviewed journal article that is not among the works named in the regulation. The other relies on a superseded edition of a compendium that is named. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The journal article is unacceptable, because the regulation does not name it.
The journal article may properly be relied upon as peer-reviewed literature.
Neither may be relied upon, since only the named works are acceptable sources.
The superseded edition remains acceptable, because the compendium is named.
The superseded edition fails, because the review must rest on current standards.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 9.17(3) provides that the review SHALL be based upon CURRENT standards, which MAY INCLUDE four named works and other peer-reviewed medical literature. The list is open, so an unnamed current source qualifies, and currency is the governing requirement, so a superseded edition of a named work does not.

choice_analysis.A: The word may include makes the list illustrative rather than closed.
choice_analysis.B: Correct: other peer-reviewed medical literature is expressly contemplated.
choice_analysis.D: Being named does not cure a lack of currency.
choice_analysis.E: Correct: the standard relied on must be current.

related_facts: The named works include Plumb's Veterinary Drug Handbook
explanation.mpje_trap: Candidates treat a named list in a regulation as a closed list of permitted sources.

reasoning_steps: Read may include as illustrative rather than exhaustive
Apply the currency requirement to each source
Assess the two sources separately on those two points
